title: Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: Unsupervised tabular anomaly detection suffers from conflicting distributional assumptions, quadratic complexity and weak handling of local anomalies; ISER addresses this by sampling psi-point subsets, building hyperspheres whose nearest-neighbour radii act as a monotonic proxy for local density, and encoding every point as a t-dimensional ensemble representation (phi = 1 - 1/r when covered, phi = 1 otherwise). Two scores are derived from that representation - the arithmetic mean (ISER-A) and the cosine similarity to the all-ones anomaly reference (ISER-S) - and the same representation is reused as a transformed feature space for an inverted-path-length Isolation Forest (ISER-IF). Averaged over 5 runs on 20 real-world datasets, ISER-S reaches the best average AUC-ROC of 0.8523 (ISER-A 0.8399) against 12 baselines, and ISER-IF improves iForest on all nine datasets in Table IV, e.g. 0.8530 -> 0.9314 on Ionosphere.

"""Data loading + evaluation utilities for the ISER reproduction.

Nothing in this file imports the authors' ISER code; it only handles
  * loading the benchmark .npz files shipped in the released repo (data/<name>.npz),
  * the AUC-ROC metric (paper R12: AUC-ROC only, higher score = more anomalous),
  * the standard iForest baseline on the raw features (Table III/IV "iForest" column).

Protocol (paper Section V-A):
  R9  - unsupervised contaminated setting: fit and score on the WHOLE dataset,
        no clean train set, no held-out split.
  R10 - every configuration is repeated 5 times with different random partitions
        and the average AUC-ROC is reported.
  R13 - the 20 published PyOD/ODDS benchmarks; here the released repo's in-tree
        copies (data/18_Ionosphere.npz = 351x32 with 126 anomalies,
        data/36_speech.npz = 3686x400 with 61 anomalies) are used.
"""

import os
import json
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA_DIR = os.path.join(HERE, "repo", "data")

# dataset name (Table II) -> released npz file name

    "Ionosphere": "18_Ionosphere.npz",
    "speech": "36_speech.npz",
    "glass": "14_glass.npz",
    "fault": "12_fault.npz",
    "Landsat": "19_landsat.npz",
    "Pima": "29_Pima.npz",
    "satellite": "30_satellite.npz",
    "vowels": "40_vowels.npz",

}

    "glass": (214, 7, 9),
    "fault": (1941, 500, 673),
    "Landsat": (6435, 36, 1333),
    "Pima": (768, 8, 268),
    "satellite": (6435, 36, 2036),
    "vowels": (1456, 12, 50),
    "WPBC": (198, 33, 47),
}


def load_dataset(name, verbose=False):
    """Load data/<name>.npz -> (X float64 (n,d), y int 0/1 with 1 = anomaly)."""
    path = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, DATASET_FILES[name])
    z = np.load(path)

"""Thin driver around the authors' released class repo/ISER.py (used verbatim).

API actually exposed by repo/ISER.py (read from the file, not assumed):

    ISER(max_samples=16, n_estimators=200, if_max_samples=256,
         random_state=None, novelty=True)
      .fit(X)          -> samples psi points w/o replacement per partitioning (R1),
                          radius = squared NN distance inside the subset (R2),
                          phi = 1 - 1/r for the smallest covering radius, 1 if
                          uncovered (R3, R4), Phi = t columns (R5),
                          then fits sklearn IsolationForest(max_samples=if_max_samples,
                          n_estimators=n_estimators) on Phi (R11)
      .transform(X)    -> (n, t) ensemble representation
      .ISER_A(X)       -> mean over the t components          (R6, higher = anomalous)
      .ISER_S(X)       -> cosine similarity of Phi to 1_t     (R7, higher = anomalous)
      .ISER_IF(X)      -> sklearn IsolationForest.decision_function(Phi).
                          sklearn's decision_function is NEGATED anomaly score
                          (higher = more inlier), which is exactly the inversion the
                          paper asks for in Section VI,
                          S_ISER-IF = 1 - 2^(-E(h(Phi))/c(n))  (R11, higher = anomalous).

repo/ISER.py imports torch at module level (line 10) although torch is never used in
the CPU path; a stub is installed in sys.modules when the real package is absent so
the authors' file is imported unmodified (no GPU needed).
"""

import os
import sys
import types
import time
import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO_DIR = os.path.join(HERE, "repo")
if REPO_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_DIR)

# torch is imported by repo/ISER.py but unused on the CPU path; stub it out if the
# heavy dependency is missing so that ISER_GPU.py / CUDA is never touched.
try:  # pragma: no cover
    import torch  # noqa: F401
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
    _stub = types.ModuleType("torch")
    _stub.__doc__ = "stub: repo/ISER.py imports torch but the CPU path never uses it"
    sys.modules["torch"] = _stub

from ISER import ISER  # noqa: E402  (authors' code, unmodified)
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score  # noqa: E402

T_DEFAULT = 200          # R8: default number of partitionings
IF_MAX_SAMPLES = 256     # ISER default / PyOD iForest subsample (A8)


def build_isr(X, psi, seed, t=T_DEFAULT, if_max_samples=IF_MAX_SAMPLES):
    """One deterministic ISER fit: psi = |Di| sampled per partitioning, seed drives
    both the partition sampling and the internal iForest (R10, A1)."""
    model = ISER(max_samples=int(psi), n_estimators=int(t),
                 if_max_samples=int(if_max_samples), random_state=int(seed))
    model.fit(X)
    return model


def scores_from_model(model, X):
    """All three scores from the SAME fitted Phi (nothing is recomputed twice)."""
    Phi = model.transform(X)
    return {
        "Phi": Phi,
        "ISER_A": np.mean(Phi, axis=1),                       # R6
        "ISER_S": np.asarray(model.ISER_S(X)).ravel(),         # R7 (authors' cosine)
        "ISER_IF": np.asarray(model.ISER_IF(X)).ravel(),       # R11
    }


def run_psi_grid(X, y, psi_values, seed_list, t=T_DEFAULT, verbose=True,
                 methods=("ISER_A", "ISER_S", "ISER_IF")):
    """Loop psi x repeat, fit once per (psi, seed), score all requested methods off
    the same Phi.  Returns per-psi per-method mean/std AUC and the diagnostics the
    intermediate checks ask for."""
    results = {m: {p: [] for p in psi_values} for m in methods}
    diag = {p: {} for p in psi_values}
    t_start = time.time()

    for psi in psi_values:
        for seed in seed_list:
            model = build_isr(X, psi, seed, t=t)
            sc = scores_from_model(model, X)
            Phi = sc["Phi"]
            assert Phi.shape == (X.shape[0], t), (psi, seed, Phi.shape)
            assert np.isfinite(Phi).all(), f"non-finite Phi at psi={psi} seed={seed}"
            for m in methods:
                v = sc[m]
                assert np.isfinite(v).all() and len(v) == X.shape[0], (m, psi, seed)
                results[m][psi].append(float(roc_auc_score(y, v)))
            if seed == seed_list[0]:
                diag[psi] = {
                    "phi_min": float(Phi.min()),
                    "phi_max": float(Phi.max()),
                    "phi_mean": float(Phi.mean()),
                    "frac_phi_eq_1": float(np.isclose(Phi, 1.0).mean()),
                }
            del model, sc, Phi
        if verbose:
            line = f"  psi={psi:4d}  " + "  ".join(
                f"{m}={np.mean(results[m][psi]):.4f}" for m in methods)
            print(line + f"   [{time.time() - t_start:.0f}s]", flush=True)

    summary = {}
    for m in methods:
        per_psi = {int(p): {"mean": float(np.mean(v)), "std": float(np.std(v)),
                            "per_seed": [float(x) for x in v]}
                   for p, v in results.items()}
        best_psi = max(per_psi, key=lambda p: per_psi[p]["mean"])
        summary[m] = {"per_psi": per_psi,
                      "best_psi": int(best_psi),
                      "best_mean_auc": per_psi[best_psi]["mean"],
                      "best_std": per_psi[best_psi]["std"],
                      "best_per_seed": per_psi[best_psi]["per_seed"]}
    return summary, diag, time.time() - t_start
